page: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a general-purpose cloud server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor with 16 shared vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 1280 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU is present on this instance.

Benchmark data positions this server consistently in the average tier across most metrics. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1451.59, and the multi-core score is 21535.52. Memory bandwidth tests show 1518.77 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 107.12 GB/sec for large-block reads. However, single-threaded gzip compression is a notable bottleneck, registering in the weak category at 23.39 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches an average score of 66.52 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations achieve 23.04 million operations per second.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff, as resources are shared with other tenants, which may introduce variability under sustained compute loads. However, the inclusion of 1280 GB of NVMe SSD storage and 64.0 GB of RAM provides a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads. This server is suited for static web serving, database operations, and lightweight language model inference, as demonstrated by its average static web serving throughput of 12.01 GB/sec and 135M model text generation speed of 115.24 tokens/sec.
description: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is an x86_64 general-purpose cloud server from the Cloud Compute family, featuring 16 shared Intel Xeon vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 1280 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating at 2.0 GHz, the processor includes AVX and AVX-512F vector extensions. Benchmark results place this server in the average performance tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 21511.0 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 21535.52. While single-threaded gzip compression is weak at 23.39 GB/sec, the server demonstrates stable average performance in other areas, including Redis SET operations at 23.04 million operations per second and static web serving at 12.01 GB/sec. The shared CPU allocation represents a tradeoff for sustained compute workloads, but the high-capacity NVMe storage and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio make it suitable for database operations, web serving, and general-purpose applications.
